full_judgment:
5. Leave was granted for consideration whether on the face of the existence of the registered sale deed dated 21.8.70 by the original lessee in favour of Md. Khalil executed much before the war of liberation and before coming into operation of PO 16 of 1972 and the same sale deed in question having got presumption of validity, the property could be taken over as an abandoned property under Article 2 of PO 16 of 1972. 

 6. From the record it appears that the case was filed by the appellant before the Court of Settlement on 10.1.88 and the hearing of the case was fixed on 27.1.88. Notice was issued on the respondent-Government to appear in this case along with all papers, documents and witnesses if there be any on that date. It further appears that no written statement was filed by the Government challenging the validity and genuineness of the sale deed, dated 21.8.70 executed by the original lessee. The case was heard and judgment was delivered on 27.1.88. From the judgment of the Court of Settlement it appears that no witnesses were examined by the parties and the Court of Settlement on a mere comparison of the signature of the original lessee Md. Hussain appearing in the kabala dated 21.8.1970 with the indenture of agreement dated 30.8.1966 found that the signature of the kabala does not tally with the signature appearing in the agreement and consequently found the kabala to be invalid and not genuine. It is to be stated that the document was registered after compliance with all the formalities of a transfer and there is no question of invalidity of the registration of the kabala in question. It was only argued by the Government that the kabala was not genuine and the court on mere comparison by its naked eyes held that the kabala is not genuine without there being any examination by the hand-writing expert or thumb impression expert to ascertain the genuineness of the thumb impression and the signature of the original lessee Md. Hussain when admittedly both these documents contain the signature and thumb impressions of the lessee. It thus appears that without affording proper and adequate opportunity to the appellant the kabala dated 21.8.70 was held to be invalid by the Court of Settlement. It may be pointed out that a registered document carries with it a presumption of validity and that presumption is a rebuttable presumption and after giving due opportunities to the parties concerned the same can be rebutted. In the present case the Court of Settlement in a very summary manner without affording adequate opportunity to the appellant to prove the genuineness of the kabala dated 20.8.1970 held the same to be invalid. The procedure adopted by the Court of Settlement being not in conformity with law and the learned Judges of the High Court Division having not at all given their attention to this material question before disposal of the writ petition, the judgments of the courts below are set aside. The appeal is allowed without any order as to cost and the same is remanded to the Court of Settlement for disposal of the case after giving adequate opportunities to the parties to prove the genuineness or otherwise of the kabala in question.
